text: News FAO and the Ministry of Agriculture validate Sector Development Plan Agreements (SDPAs) strengthening public engagement in policy development By developing local capacities, building trust, and fostering collaboration between market players and institutions, these agreements show how structured value chains can generate sustainable economic well-being and boost employment and transform agrifood systems. Participants from various value chains listening to consultants presentations and engaging during the SDPA's validation workshop in Manzini. ©FAO/ThabisoMnisi Manzini, Eswatini - In the framework of supporting the accelerated implementation of food systems transformation pathways in Eswatini, the Ministry of Agriculture, with support from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), convened key stakeholders to validate the Sector Development Plan Agreements (SDPAs) for the honey, poultry, coffee, banana, and piggery value chains. The Government of Eswatini considers coffee a strategic agribusiness with the potential to promote employment and improve the economic well-being of smallholder farmers. Notwithstanding the sector’s expansion, persistent and adverse market imbalances, coupled with asymmetric income distribution among market participants, pose a significant threat to the sustenance of smallholder producers. The validation workshop brought together farmers, private sector actors, financial institutions, and policymakers to align priorities and strengthen crucial partnerships. Participants engaged in invaluable dialogue to validate recommendations focusing on enhancing production and infrastructure development, strengthening input supply such as breeding stock and beehive equipment, improving extension services, and facilitating access to finance. These plans aim to address persistent market imbalances and high input costs, enabling stringent quality control across production, processing, and packaging - contributing to boosted agricultural productivity and improved livelihoods for smallholder farmers. The framework of the Sector Development Plan Agreements is most effective when it is anchored in evidence-based policy actions and strong market collaboration at country-level. Recognizing honey and pig production as strategic agribusiness ventures, overcoming challenges such as uneven income distribution is critical to supporting the most vulnerable smallholder producers in a sustainable manner. By developing local capacities, building trust, and fostering collaboration between market players and institutions, these agreements show how structured value chains can generate sustainable economic well-being and boost employment across the agricultural sector. “The strategic objective of validating these SDPAs is to assist smallholder farmers in building unity, cohesion, and a unified voice when dealing with pressing challenges, and to help them receive targeted support for the various value chains. The Government of Eswatini is in a process of engaging in a meaningful way with sectors that are organized and representative of producers and industry players. To build an environment where specific sectors can develop strategies to improve production, marketing and targeted investments, and even develop programmes for these value chains,” said Khanyakwezwe Dlamini, Planning Officer and National Project Coordinator, Ministry of Agriculture. Speaking at the validation workshop, Howard Mbuyisa, Assistant FAO Representative highlighted the strategic importance of the initiative, “The validation of the honey and piggery value chain SDPA’s marks a milestone towards enhancing production, marketing, and investment in these vital sectors. Establishing this evidence-based framework is essential to empowering smallholders in production, productivity, and investment, ensuring an inclusive and transformative journey within Eswatini's agrifood systems.” Moving forward, the successful implementation of these SDPAs will rely on sustained commitment and active participation from all stakeholders involved. The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with FAO, plans to establish a robust monitoring and evaluation mechanism to track progress, ensure accountability, and adapt strategies to emerging challenges. In line with its unique mandate to eliminate hunger and improve rural livelihoods, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) shares a steadfast commitment to establishing robust agricultural frameworks. Through this ongoing partnership, FAO has successfully supported the Ministry of Agriculture in developing 12 SDPAs to date, championing a proactive and structured approach to transforming agrifood systems and securing a resilient future for farmers.
